answer: Since the dawn index is rebuilt each epoch, the horizon audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, because the tide embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator burns authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 74% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. That is 11 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
